sourceBaseline: 005852a2 (pushed dev commit of Fast Checks run 40232090301); git blob b5a88d17a277d0c33e2b15d6af46de940eaad313
originalFailure: Fast Checks run 40232090301, job 121285780064 'Agent Tools Shard 2' (audit shard index 1 of 6, ubuntu-24.04 image 20261012.334.1, x86_64, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, CPython 3.12.15): FAIL at line 314 after 0.0092 s. The case's 'python -I -B -c' child exited 1 with no output and 'SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 22)'.
originalFailureTrace: SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 22)
originalFailureLogScope: gh run view 40232090301 --log --job 121285780064 output (the complete Agent Tools Shard 2 job log); the trace above is its excerpt with the job, step and timestamp prefixes removed.
earlierFailureEventsScope: artifact agent-test-shard-40187427911-1-1/events.jsonl of Fast Checks run 40187427911 at cc2873b5, whose shard timed out before unittest printed tracebacks. The case's generated program is byte-identical at 60bb1a26, cc2873b5 and 005852a2, so that unexplained 0.013 s failure is the same compile error.
confirmedCause: The case wrote its child program in a non-raw triple-quoted literal (code = """..."""). Python therefore turned the escape child's intended pid terminator, the two characters backslash and n in os.write(write,(str(os.getpid())+'\n').encode()), into a real line break before the program reached the child, so the one-line string literal on program line 22 was left unterminated. python -c compiles the whole program before it runs any of it, so the child exited 1 within milliseconds, before the fixture loaded and before any subreaper, PIDfd or /proc facility was used. The case has failed this way on every Linux run since it was added in 60bb1a26; its class is skipped off Linux, so no Darwin run reached it.
fix: The case's program literal is raw (code = r"""..."""), as in its descriptor sibling, so the child receives the intended escape and writes its pid followed by a newline. Every other program byte, the authenticated OWNED_DESCENDANT_SOURCE fixture and its cleanup_selftest are unchanged; that fixture's own generated sources were already escaped correctly.
controlledRegression: agent_tools.tests.test_android_owned_descendant_child_syntax runs the original case of this whole beforeimage (compiled from these bytes in a private module whose __file__ is the current module's) and of the current module. The beforeimage case runs unchanged; the class's Linux-only skip is bypassed because the child rejects the program before any Linux facility. Both cases also hand their exact argv to the real interpreter with only the fixture argument replaced by an owned probe that prints its argv and exits as soon as the program runs, and the exact programs are compiled in process as python -c compiles them.
failingEvidence: Unfixed: the beforeimage case fails at line 314 with exactly the CI message on this Darwin host under CPython 3.14.3 and 3.12.13 (returncode=1, empty stdout, the four-line SyntaxError at program line 22 with the same caret column); under the probe the child exits 1 with that SyntaxError and the probe never runs; in process the program raises SyntaxError at line 22. With the unfixed module as the current one (an owned clone of 005852a2 plus this regression), the regression fails at its GREEN assertion on both interpreters: that child also exits 1 with the same SyntaxError.
passingEvidence: Fixed: the same probe run exits 0 with only the probe line, proving the real interpreter accepted the complete program and began running it; it compiles in process; and the fixed program equals the beforeimage program with only that line break replaced by the intended escape. On CPython 3.14.3 and 3.12.13, also with FORCE_COLOR=1 and under the sandboxed runner, the syntax controls pass; an escape-only fix ('\\n' in the non-raw literal) passes too, while a dropped pid terminator or any other program drift fails.
routineSuite: agent_tools.tests.test_android_owned_descendant_child_syntax runs in the affected agent-test stage of the managed pre-push tier and the Fast Checks agent shards whenever the selector reaches it, including changes to test_android_launcher_version_source_snapshot.py, its fixture module, this beforeimage or this provenance. The Linux case runs whenever its own module or fixture changes.
nativeEvidenceLimit: Hosted-runner test-harness outcome only; no Android device, emulator, debugger, VM or native host is involved or claimed. The probe stops the fixed program at its fixture load, so the subreaper, PIDfd and /proc behaviour of the fixed case, and therefore its GREEN outcome, is confirmed only by OwnedDescendantLinuxTests on the next Linux Fast Checks run.

timeoutDiagnostics.failureType: Bare timeout report. The case called subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, timeout=8) without handling subprocess.TimeoutExpired. The separate-session middle and escape children that cleanup_selftest forks sleep 10 s and inherit the child's output pipes, so a refusal between that fork and their SIGKILL in close_descendants (the 2 s select, the pid format check, a collect_descendants identity, boot, PIDfd or scope refusal, or the process-group check) keeps those pipes open past the timeout. The case then failed as a bare TimeoutExpired: the child's error stayed only in the exception's captured output, which unittest does not print, and no host facts were reported.
timeoutDiagnostics.discovery: Review of the syntax fix. No CI run reached this path, because the case never ran past compilation, so there is no CI failure trace. It was reproduced locally on Darwin under CPython 3.14.3 with the case's real method, the real subprocess.run and timeout=8, changing only the fixture argument to a probe that forks a setsid sleeper and then raises ValueError('debugger_descendant_identity_unknown').
timeoutDiagnostics.unfixedSource: This beforeimage with only its program literal made raw (code = r"""), that is the syntax fix alone. It is byte-identical to the reviewed syntax-fix module and keeps the beforeimage's own call and failure reporting unchanged.
timeoutDiagnostics.originalFailureEvidence: With a 10 s sleeper the unfixed case failed after 8.0 s with subprocess.TimeoutExpired, and its report contained neither the child's ValueError nor host facts, while error.stderr held the ValueError. With 5 s sleepers (the case's own second-phase values) the pipes closed before the timeout and the AssertionError report was complete.
timeoutDiagnostics.fix: The case catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired from its unchanged call (same argv, program, capture_output=True and timeout=8) and fails from it with self.failureException carrying the timeout, the captured partial stdout and stderr and host_facts(); the TimeoutExpired stays chained as the cause. This explicit failure also works before Python 3.11, where an add_note form would raise AttributeError and hide the output again.
timeoutDiagnostics.controlledRegression: GeneratedChildProgramRegression.test_descendant_held_pipes_timeout_reports_child_error_and_host_facts runs the original case of the unfixed source above (derived in process from this beforeimage and checked against the digest above) and of the current module with their exact call, with only the fixture argument replaced by an owned probe and the timeout shortened to 2 s for the real subprocess.run. The probe's OWNED_DESCENDANT_SOURCE forks a separate-session descendant that holds the inherited output pipes until the control closes a release pipe, then raises the refusal. Both runs really time out with the refusal captured, EOF on a pipe that only the descendant still holds proves that it exited, and only the failure report differs.
timeoutDiagnostics.failingEvidence: In an owned clone whose current module is the unfixed source above, the control fails at its GREEN assertion on CPython 3.14.3, 3.12.13 and 3.10.20, because the report is the bare TimeoutExpired. With the 005852a2 module as the current one it fails earlier, because that program does not compile.
timeoutDiagnostics.passingEvidence: Fixed: the control passes on CPython 3.10.20, 3.11.15, 3.12.13, 3.13.13, 3.14.3 and 3.14.5, with FORCE_COLOR=1 and under the sandboxed runner, and no probe process remains. Of ten variants of the case's handling, the fix and an implicit self.fail form pass, and an add_note form passes on 3.12 but fails on 3.10. Missing stderr or host facts, only the last stderr line, a repr dump, a bare re-raise, a swallowed timeout and timeout=9 all fail.
timeoutDiagnostics.routineSuite: The same module and change-scoped selection as the syntax regression.
timeoutDiagnostics.nativeEvidenceLimit: Local processes only; the probe stands in for cleanup_selftest's descendants. Whether the fixed Linux case refuses at all, and its subreaper, PIDfd and /proc behaviour, are confirmed only by OwnedDescendantLinuxTests on Linux CI. If it times out there, its report now carries the child's output and the host facts.
